title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier (with at most one automated repair) increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Each pair evaluated one shared_initial candidate under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable marginal rescue by the guarded pipeline. We archive all preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and emphasize that the reported inference applies to the preregistered shared_initial estimand that conditions on a single LLM draw per intent.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. Operators require semantic guarantees—sequencing, reachability, and policy preservation—that syntactic checks alone cannot provide. Hybrid architectures pairing generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) aim to reduce operational risk, but the measurable benefit depends on the evaluand (what is held fixed), the generator's single‑shot quality, validator expressiveness, and permitted repair budget.

We preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) to quantify the deterministic rescue achievable when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced a single shared_initial candidate using the declared generator (gpt-5-mini) and compared: (a) baseline — accept the single candidate without repair, and (b) guarded — run a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and allow at most one automated repair which itself is re‑validated. The core research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same single candidate without repair?

Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a shared_initial estimand that conditions on a single LLM draw per intent; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the single automated repair transcript archived with the run; (3) an artifact‑grounded interpretation of estimator conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.

Terminology note. Throughout the paper we use 'shared_initial' to indicate the single LLM generation per intent that is reused for both baseline and guarded conditions; 'guarded' denotes deterministic validation plus a bounded repair budget (≤1 automated repair), and 'baseline' denotes accepting the shared_initial candidate without modification.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and systems papers document active efforts to apply LLMs to NetOps problems including intent translation, configuration synthesis, automated repair, and tool‑augmented orchestration [https://openalex.org/W4402742293; https://openalex.org/W4411015066; https://openalex.org/W4416927413]. Architectures that interpose validators or tools (planner‑centric frameworks, ReAct variants, and generate→validate→repair pipelines) are proposed to reduce hallucination and semantic errors; empirical gains reported by prior work vary with validator coverage and generation strategy [doi:10.1609/aaai.v40i40.40676; https://openalex.org/W4404240614].

Two methodological gaps motivate this study. First, many prior comparisons conflate deterministic validator rescue with benefits obtained by drawing multiple independent model candidates: permitting resampling mixes generator variance effects with deterministic validator effects. Second, community adoption of benchmarks that emphasize semantic correctness (reachability, policy compliance) rather than only syntactic validity remains limited [https://openalex.org/W4415071524; https://openalex.org/W4392875514]. Our paired shared_initial design isolates deterministic rescue from resampling effects and thereby provides an operationally relevant bound for policies that limit model calls per change request.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study preregistration (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) fixed the primary estimand as the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded minus baseline) computed on paired cases that evaluate the same shared_initial candidate. Confirmatory design elements were frozen prior to main execution: planned analyzable pairs N = 300 (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high), explicit inclusion/exclusion rules, the binary scoring rule (unflagged == pass), and the analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The preregistration included an optional pilot (n = 60) for discordance estimation; that pilot was not executed and no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed. This deviation is recorded in the preregistration archive and is stated in the Disclosure Statement.

Task generation and synthetic suite. Tasks were produced deterministically by the registered task generator into a synthetic_topology_suite and stratified into difficulty bins using generator metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count). Representative difficulty patterns include shutdown_configure_restore (medium) and paired_link_atomic_mtu_change (hard). The task manifest records required_sequences and intent constraints for every item; the synthetic suite enforces protected_interface invariants and preserve_unspecified_state rules that the validator checks.

Shared_initial protocol and generator. To implement the shared_initial estimand the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial generation per pair and reused that identical candidate for both baseline and guarded conditions. The declared generator for shared_initial candidate production was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records requested_model = "gpt-5-mini"). The shared_initial protocol isolates deterministic validator/repair rescue from gains achievable by allowing independent resampling, verifier‑driven steering, or iterative generation; this design reflects operational policies that constrain model calls for cost, latency, or governance reasons.

Validator, scoring, and repair operator. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule: deterministic checks for sequencing invariants (must_be_down_for_fields), required_command_count, preservation of unspecified state, reachability invariants encoded in the synthetic topology, and forbidden‑template protection (protected_interfaces). Scoring is binary (unflagged == pass). The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair attempt (repair budget ≤1). The repair routine is a constrained edit operator limited to localized sequencing or insertion edits; it logs a repair provider trace and is applied only if the validator flags the shared_initial candidate. A candidate that remains flagged after the permitted repair attempt counts as a failure for the primary estimand.

Contamination controls, negative controls, and stopping rules. The preregistered contamination controls included one intentionally broken negative control per complexity stratum and deterministic invariant checks (pre/post reachability matrices). Per preregistration, pairs with both calls failing due to provider/infrastructure outages would be excluded; none occurred. The preregistration also specified a stopping rule to halt if >20% dual-call exclusions occurred; that did not trigger during execution.

Execution instrumentation and audit. The confirmatory run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter under execution_mode scientific_confirmatory. Execution audit values (from the execution manifest): planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 600, complete_pair_count = 300, model_calls_used = 301, maximum_model_calls = 600. Provider call auditing recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 301 and stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 1. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode and provider‑call accounting and reports all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true. These deterministic audit values are archived to permit third‑party verification of accounting and stage counts.

Analysis executor and inference. The preregistered analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 computed paired contingency counts (n11,n10,n01,n00), the absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline), an exact two‑sided McNemar test, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI. Bootstrap parameters used in the archived analysis are seed = 1729 and resamples B = 10000. Sensitivity analyses described in the preregistration (failure‑as‑zero treatments and stratum‑wise tests with FDR control) are exploratory and archived; the confirmatory test reported here follows the preregistered primary analysis plan.
sections.results:
Execution integrity and accounting. The hosted adapter completed the confirmatory run with completed_episode_count = 600 and complete_pair_count = 300. Provider and stage auditing show hosted_model_call_event_count = 301 (300 shared_initial generations + 1 repair call). The deterministic reconciliation artifact records baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 and confirms pair accounting (n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0) with all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 299/300 (0.9966666666666667), guarded successes = 300/300 (1.0). The paired contingency is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test returned p = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333333333332993. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI computed with B = 10000 resamples and seed = 1729 yields [0.00, 0.01]. Per‑stratum totals: low stratum 100/100 baseline & guarded; medium 100/100 baseline & guarded; high stratum baseline 99/100 vs guarded 100/100.

Repair diagnostic. The single discordant episode (the lone n10) invoked the allowed automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial flag to an omitted sequencing command required by the intent (a must_be_down_for_fields violation): the shared_initial candidate lacked the required 'admin down' prior to a VLAN/MTU change. The constrained repair inserted the missing sequencing command and the deterministic validator subsequently reported valid == true. The archived run bundle contains the low‑level repair provider trace and the validator trace for this episode; the manuscript reports a concise semantic summary here rather than reproducing full provider transcripts in the body.

Contamination and missingness. The contamination_summary.csv in the archive is empty and analysis/missingness_summary.csv shows no excluded or failed episodes (all zeros for failed and unscorable episodes). No pairs were excluded under the preregistered rules and no provider/infrastructure outage exclusions occurred during the confirmatory run.

Statistical interpretation. The near‑ceiling baseline produced only a single discordant pair, which limits inferential sensitivity: the exact McNemar p‑value of 1.0 reflects the paucity of discordant evidence under the shared_initial estimand. The bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute paired improvement at ≤1 percentage point in this experimental context. These inferential results apply strictly to the preregistered estimand, the fixed repair budget (≤1), the synthetic topology suite sampled by the deterministic task generator, and the declared generator (gpt-5-mini).
sections.discussion:
Estimand and operational alignment. Conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent (shared_initial) corresponds to operational policies that limit model calls per change request (e.g., cost or latency constraints). Under such policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. Workflows that allow resampling, verifier‑guided generation, or interactive steering change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates because they exploit generator variance; those workflows must be evaluated under a different preregistered estimand that permits independent alternate draws.

Ceiling effects and the unexecuted pilot. The preregistration targeted detection of a 10 percentage‑point absolute improvement with planned power ≈0.8, relying on pilot‑estimated discordance. Because the optional pilot (n = 60) intended to estimate discordance was not executed, the main run confronted a near‑ceiling baseline (299/300), producing minimal discordance (m = 1) and reduced power to detect small absolute differences. This underscores the practical value of small calibration pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling on chosen task suites.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The observed single failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, forbidden ACL removal) were not observed at scale on this synthetic suite. The marginal utility of a guarded pipeline therefore depends on (a) the deployment distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness. A richer validator or a synthetic distribution biased toward reachability or ACL invariants could increase observed rescue rates. Conversely, if operator risk policies disallow automated edits, the guarded pipeline's deterministic rescue becomes operationally limited to detection and human escalation.

Repair budget and bounded edits. We purposely limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to measure bounded deterministic rescue. That design measured only localized sequencing corrections; iterative repair, larger edit operators, or interactive verifier‑guided generation would increase rescue opportunities but test a different estimand. The archived repair trace for the single rescued episode allows detailed follow‑up analyses of repair patterns and edit efficacy.

Threats to validity. Internal validity risks include prompt sensitivity, generator nondeterminism under different temperature settings, and the choice to condition on a single draw. Construct validity concerns whether the binary unflagged scoring rule and the synthetic validator capture real operational risk (reachability and policy semantics). External validity is limited by the use of a single model (gpt-5-mini), one validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a synthetic task suite; results may differ on production topologies, alternate LLMs, or richer validators. Conclusion validity is constrained by the near‑ceiling baseline and the consequent low discordant count; small absolute effects below the bootstrap CI upper bound cannot be excluded.

Operational recommendation. Organizations should align the evaluation estimand with operational constraints: if policies permit multiple model calls or interactive steering, allow resampling or verifier‑guided generation during evaluation to measure rescue achievable by exploiting generator variance. If model calls are constrained, the shared_initial estimand provides an operationally meaningful upper bound for deterministic verifier/repair rescue applied to a single candidate.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). Deterministic validator+repair rescued a single sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity to small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived with the study id to enable reproducibility and targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, or repair budget.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
